# User guide: Run an agent from a script

## In plain words

A script on your server can ask the plugin to start an agent. The script says which agent, which folder and what to do. The plugin opens a workspace, gives the agent the task and shows an Unraid notice. The plugin checks which script asked. It starts only the scripts that you put on a list called **Authorised scripts**. A read-only run starts at once. A run that may change files waits until you approve it in the Activity tray.

Words used on this page:

- **Run**: one call from a script, and the workspace that the plugin opens for it.
- **Fingerprint**: a short code that the plugin computes from the content of a script file (a sha256 hash). A changed file has another fingerprint.
- **Activity tray**: the pill at the bottom right of the page that lists what the plugin is doing.
- **Read-only**: the agent may use only the tools Read, Grep and Glob and the read tools of the plugin. It has no shell and no file editing, the plugin tools that change things are denied, and the file tools stay in the run folder, the agent ignores the settings files of that folder, and it can still report its result. The agent still runs as root, and these limits come from the agent itself. They are not a lock on the disks.

## Where to find it

- **Settings, Configuration** tab, card **Script runs**: the switch, the list of Authorised scripts and, in the part **Advanced**, the limits.
- **Activity tray**: shows each run, each refused script and each run that started (a read-only run shows here as started) and each run that may change files and waits for your approval.
- Unraid's own notices: a notice appears when a run starts and when a script is refused.

## How to use it

### Turn the feature on and add a script

1. Open **Settings**, then the **Configuration** tab.
2. Open the card **Script runs**. Set **Let scripts start agent runs** to **On**. The default is **Off (default)**.
3. Under **Authorised scripts**, press **Add a script**.
4. Type the full path of the script file. Type the agents it may start, for example `claude-code`, and the folders it may use, one on each line.
5. Press **Save**. Expect: the script appears in the list with a fingerprint.

### Call the plugin from the script

A script runs the command `aicli-run` as root. For example:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
aicli-run --agent=claude-code --folder=/mnt/cache/appdata/example \
  --prompt="Look into the finding in the data below." \
  --title="Daily check" --key=daily-check --data-file=/tmp/finding.json
```

The command prints one JSON object. The field `state` says what happened. The exit code of the command says the same in a number: 0 started, 2 bad input, 3 the feature is off, 4 not run as root, 20 waits for approval (a run that may change files), 21 refused, 22 duplicate, 23 held.

### Approve an unknown or changed script

1. A script that is not on the list is refused. The plugin adds one item to the **Activity tray** and shows an Unraid notice.
2. Read the path, the fingerprint and the request in the item.
3. Press **Approve** to put the script on the list as a read-only script. Each later read-only call of this script then starts the agent at once, with no further approval, up to the runs a day that the entry allows. Press **Reject** to turn it away.
4. Expect: the next call of the script starts. The call that was refused does not start by itself.

A script whose file changed is refused in the same way, until you approve the new fingerprint. The old limits stay.

### Runs that need approval

A read-only call starts at once. It needs no approval, and it still counts against the limits. The **Activity tray** shows it as **Run started**. A call with `--mode=may-change` waits in the **Activity tray** as **Approve run**. The item shows the script, the agent, the folder, the mode and the full task. Press **Approve** to start the run. A run with `--mode=may-change` then works without asking for permission, when the agent has such a mode. A read-only run keeps its permission questions and all its read-only limits. Before it starts, the plugin checks again that the script is still on the list with the same fingerprint, that the file is unchanged and that the limits still allow the run. With no answer in the time you set, the run ends and starts nothing.

## Choices and settings

| Setting | What it does | Default | When to change it |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Let scripts start agent runs** | The master switch. Off refuses every call. | Off (default) | Turn it on when you add your first script. |
| **Authorised scripts** | The scripts that may call, each with its agents, folders, highest mode and runs each day. | Empty | Add a script for each job. |
| **Runs open at one time** | The most runs that are open together. | 2 | Raise it when scripts often overlap. |
| **Runs each day** (all scripts) | The most runs that start in 24 hours. | 6 | Raise it for a busy server. |
| **Wait before the same problem runs again** | Hours before a call with the same key starts a new run. | 24 | Lower it for a problem that needs a quick second look. |
| **Time to approve a run** | Hours that you have to approve a run that may change files. | 24 | Raise it if you check the tray rarely. |
| **Notify me when a run starts** | An Unraid notice at the start of a run. Warnings always show. | Yes (default) | Turn it off for a script that runs often. |

## What happens behind the scenes

The plugin finds the calling script from the process list of the server, not from what the caller says. It compares the content of the file with the stored fingerprint. This protects you from a mistake, a stray script and a changed script. It does not protect you from a hostile program that runs as root, because such a program can fake its name. See C4 Code: Services (part 3 of 3) for the technical detail.

The plugin reads the script from the file that the shell has open, and it looks only at the program directly above the command. A program that a listed script started is not that script. The plugin writes the task into a folder named `.aicli-task` inside the folder of the run, so a read-only run does add that one folder there. The data of a call goes to a private file in the plugin's own state folder, and the task names that file. The agent does not inherit the environment of the script.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| Exit code 3 | The switch is off. | Turn on **Let scripts start agent runs**. |
| Exit code 21 and an item in the **Activity tray** | The script is new or its file changed. | Read the item and press **Approve** or **Reject**. |
| Exit code 21 with a sentence about a limit | The call asked for more than the list allows. | Change the limits of the script under **Authorised scripts**, or change the call. |
| Exit code 21, "No script file was found" | Someone typed the command in a shell, or used a pipe. | Put the command in a script file and add the file to the list. |
| Exit code 22 | A run with the same key is open, or started a short time ago. | Wait, or use another key. |
| Exit code 23 | A limit on runs, or the usage limit of the agent, holds the call. | Call again later. |
| The list shows "THE FILE CHANGED" | The file differs from the stored fingerprint. | Open **Edit**, tick **Trust the file as it is now** and press **Save**, if you made the change. |

This version runs every agent as root. A restricted run user, a temporary folder for a run, the final report of a run and a wait option come in later versions.
